Deprecation Notice:
The Marketing Version 202601 (Marketing January 2026) will be sunset on January 15, 2027. We recommend that you migrate to the latest versioned APIs to avoid disruptions. For information on all the supported versions, refer to the migrations documentation.
If you haven’t yet migrated and have questions, submit a request on the LinkedIn Developer Support Portal.
Starting with version 202611, you can retrieve an existing boost, update its targeting and political declaration, or delete it through dedicated management resources.

Use a member OAuth access token and include Linkedin-Version: 202611 and X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0. The path key is the numeric campaign ID, not a campaign URN. For example, use 222222222 from urn:li:sponsoredCampaign:222222222.
The authenticated member must be authorized to manage the boost in the selected context.
Use Status to look up the campaign and account URNs for the post. Post also returns them when the boost is created. Send a GET to the appropriate management resource.

Rows.Text: The numeric campaign ID in the resource path.
The URL-encoded boosted ugcPost or share URN.

Blocks.Text: For example, a response can contain:

Send a Rest.li partial update using HTTP POST, X-RestLi-Method: PARTIAL_UPDATE, and a patch body. Both management resources require the account query parameter. Unlike Company Page GET, update doesn't require organization or targetPost query parameters.
Only targetingCriteria and politicalIntent are editable. Budget, objective, schedule, and other system-managed fields aren't editable through this resource.

When changing targeting, always send targetingCriteria.type and the complete desired includeAll list, including a location. If type is USER_AUDIENCE, also send the saved-audience id. Omit excludeAny to keep the campaign's existing exclusions, or send excludeAny: [] to clear them. To replace exclusions, send the desired excludeAny list. An exclusions-only targeting update still requires type, id when applicable, and includeAll with a location.
Keep interface locale targeting consistent with the campaign's locale. Changing the criteria's name doesn't rename a saved audience; use Edit an audience for that operation.

Retrieve the current boost before previewing a targeting update. If the management patch omits excludeAny to preserve exclusions, explicitly include the current boost's excludeAny list in the Hydrate request, together with the proposed inclusion rules. Hydrate must preview the effective audience that Manage will save; omitting existing exclusions from the preview can change the forecast and political declaration requirement. When clearing or replacing exclusions, preview the same empty or replacement list that you send in the patch.

Preview the chosen targeting through Hydrate before saving and collect a political declaration when required. For EU targeting, display the mandatory consent using the required wording and presentation, clearly presented and checked by default before submitting the targeting change. Sending NOT_POLITICAL alone doesn't satisfy the consent requirement. An absent politicalDeclarationRequired field isn't a confirmed false. A successful management update isn't proof that a declaration isn't required. LinkedIn prohibits political advertising.

The management patch uses a direct enum string, such as "politicalIntent":"NOT_POLITICAL", unlike Post's {"value":"NOT_POLITICAL"} action parameter. Omitting politicalIntent preserves the current declaration. Don't delete targetingCriteria or politicalIntent with $delete.
Important
Political intent declaration is a legal requirement when targeting EU countries. For more information, see Political advertising in the European Union.

Declaring POLITICAL doesn't itself end the boost or prevent managing and updating the campaign. This API behavior doesn't override LinkedIn's prohibition on political advertising or imply approval to serve the ad.
This example uses USER_AUDIENCE with saved-audience ID 12345 and preserves existing exclusions by omitting excludeAny.

http


curl

For a Company Page boost, use /rest/organizationBoostManage/222222222?account=urn%3Ali%3AsponsoredAccount%3A987654321 with the same headers and body. Replace the sample account, campaign, saved-audience ID, and targeting with the boost's actual values.
A successful update returns 204 No Content with no body. Retrieve the boost again to verify its saved configuration.
DELETE removes the boost; it doesn't pause it. Both resources require account. Company Page DELETE doesn't require an organization query parameter.

http


curl

DELETE https://api.linkedin.com/rest/organizationBoostManage/222222222?account=urn%3Ali%3AsponsoredAccount%3A987654321
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
Linkedin-Version: 202611
X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0

curl -X DELETE 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/organizationBoostManage/222222222?account=urn%3Ali%3AsponsoredAccount%3A987654321' \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {access_token}' \
-H 'Linkedin-Version: 202611' \
-H 'X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0'
For a member boost, use /rest/memberBoostManage/222222222?account=urn%3Ali%3AsponsoredAccount%3A987654321 instead.
A successful deletion returns 204 No Content with no body. Authorization and campaign deletion restrictions still apply.
Version 202610 uses Init with campaignUrn and accountUrn to load existing boost details, and memberBoostCampaign or organizationBoostCampaign to delete a boost.

In version 202611, both Member and Company Page Init continue to accept optional campaignUrn and accountUrn action parameters. Init returns lifecycle status when a campaign is supplied, and campaignUrn can be present in the response. These Init fields remain supported.

The legacy memberBoostCampaign and organizationBoostCampaign delete resources are deprecated but remain available in versions 202610 and 202611. For version 202611 and later, use DELETE /rest/memberBoostManage/{campaignId} or DELETE /rest/organizationBoostManage/{campaignId}, with the required account query parameter.

Rows.Text: Malformed account, post, or organization input; malformed patch; or deletion of targetingCriteria or politicalIntent.
Correct the input described in the response. Use $set for editable fields.
A targeting update omits type, omits id when type is USER_AUDIENCE, or omits includeAll with a location.
Include the required targeting fields, even when changing only exclusions.
The caller isn't authorized for the boost.
Check the permission and member's access to the selected context and account.
The service can't find a referenced entity.
Verify the campaign, account, and, for GET, post and organization.
A management precondition isn't met, or an entity conflicts with the operation.
Resolve the condition described in the service message before retrying.
The service can't complete the request.
Retry later; contact Developer Support if it persists.

Blocks.Text: Authentication and rate-limit failures can also occur before the management operation runs. Use a valid token and respect retry guidance in rate-limit responses.
